messages:
alex: FYI customer reported sudden mTLS failures to our Private control plane (controlplane.int.redwood) right after their proxy vendor pushed firmware v3.2.1 at ~08:10 PST. Symptoms: immediate RSTs and TLS alert 40. They attached packet capture and proxy config.

maria: Thanks. Can you paste the openssl s_client command they used and a small tcpdump excerpt? Also need egress IP list and the exact FQDN they hit.

alex: They hit controlplane.int.redwood:443 via corporate proxy (proxy internal 10.8.0.22 -> NAT egress 54.21.33.11). Repro command from their jump host:
```
openssl s_client -connect controlplane.int.redwood:443 -tls1_3 -alpn h2 -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile ca-bundle.pem -msg
```
tcpdump snippet shows client SYN then immediate RST from egress:
```
08:10:11.001 IP 10.8.0.55.52344 > 54.21.33.11.443: Flags [S], seq 0
08:10:11.002 IP 54.21.33.11.443 > 10.8.0.55.52344: Flags [R], seq 0
```
Proxy logs: "forwarded client cert" but note: proxy config has ssl_certificate_chain set to leaf only.

sam: From our side we see Alert 40 and an X509 verify error. Handshake fails when server sees incomplete client chain (Verify return code 21). Also saw a flurry of DENY hits on our firewall for ephemeral ports 32768-32780 from 54.21.33.11 during the same minute. Their proxy NAT appears to be using a small ephemeral range which some network middleboxes are blocking.

priya: Typical culprits for this pattern:
- Proxy/NGFW that terminates and re-issues TLS, but misconfigures chain forwarding -> intermediate CA missing -> verify error 21 -> TLS Alert 40
- Egress NAT that rewrites or restricts source ports (ephemeral port preservation) -> server sees invalid/mangled flow -> immediate RST
Ask them to: (1) dump full s_client cert output (show chain + verify), (2) ensure proxy is configured to forward full cert chain (include intermediates), (3) widen NAT ephemeral mappings or preserve source ports, (4) temporarily allow 54.21.33.11/32 to controlplane:443 for repro.

alex: They emailed back with s_client verify block:
```
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=client.example
 1 s:/CN=intermediate-ca
---
verify error:num=21:unable to verify the first certificate
---
TLS alert number 40
```
Also attached proxy fragment: `ssl_certificate_chain: client.crt` (no intermediates). Vendor FW change log mentions "new default to strip intermediates" in v3.2.1.

maria: Ok good repro. Can we get them to add the intermediate to the proxy’s ssl_certificate_chain and open ephemeral range 32768-61000 in the NAT/firewall for the test window?

alex: They patched proxy to include intermediate chain and widened NAT. After change, s_client shows:
```
verify return:1
Verify return code: 0 (ok)
SSL-Session:
    Protocol  : TLSv1.3
    Cipher    : TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
```
No more RSTs, API calls to control plane succeed. Customer confirmed services restored. :tada:

sam: For the runbook, when seeing Alert 40 or instant RSTs from customer side, check in order:
1) client cert chain completeness (ask for s_client cert dump)
2) proxy/inspection device behaviour (does it strip intermediates or re-issue certs?)
3) egress NAT/source-port preservation and ephemeral ranges
4) firewall rules that may deny ephemeral ranges to controlplane
5) DNS resolution (A vs AAAA vs ALIAS) if packet shows unexpected path
Add these steps to support checklist and include example s_client/curl commands.

priya: Also note: some proxies will choose IPv6 or alternate IP from DNS ALIAS which can hit a different NAT path. If possible ask for a `curl -v --resolve controlplane.int.redwood:443:<expected-ip>` repro to rule out DNS path variance.

maria: Closing the ticket with remediation steps and vendor escalation note (firmware default removed intermediates). Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
